sections.label: Pallavi
sections.ta:
முகுந்தன் மூத்தவளே முண்டக விழி உருவே
முண்டாசுர மர்த்தினியே மூவுலகின் மூலாதாரமே
sections.translit:
mukundhan mUtthavaLE muNdaga vizhi uruvE
muNdAsura marddhiniyE mUvulagin mUlAdhAramE
sections.en: Oh elder sister of Lord Mukunda, you have lovely, lotus-shaped eyes. You are the slayer of the demon Mundasura and the source of the three worlds.

sections.label: Anupallavi
sections.ta:
முப்பத்து முக்கோடி தேவரும் முத்தொழில் மூவரும்
முனைந்து உபாசிக்கும் முக்கண்ணன் மனோகரியே
sections.translit:
muppatthu mukkOdi dhEvarum mutthozhil mUvarum
munaindhu upAsikkum mukkaNNan manOgariyE
sections.en: You are the beloved of the three-eyed Siva, and all thirty-three crore celestials—as well as the divine Trinity responsible for creation, preservation, and destruction. They worship you with deep devotion.

sections.label: Charanam
sections.ta:
முகிலாய் வந்து மாயை புரிந்து பார்த்தனைக் காத்தாய்
முதலும் முடிவும் உணர்த்தி கம்சனைக் கலங்க வைத்தாய்
மும்முலை தாங்கி முடியும் சூடி முத்தமிழ் வளர்த்தாய்
முத்தொடி கரத்தினால் மூலவன் கண்ட நஞ்சினை முறித்தாய்
sections.translit:
mugilAy vandhu mAyai purindhu pArtthanaik kAtthAy
mudhalum mudivum uNartthi kamsanaik kalanga vaitthAy
mummulai thAngi mudiyum sUdi mutthamizh vaLartthAy
mutthodi karatthinAl mUlavan kaNta nanjinai muRitthAy
sections.en: You appeared as a patch of cloud, performed an illusion, and protected Arjuna on the battlefield. You revealed both the beginning and the end to the demon Kamsa and struck terror into his heart. You had three breasts early in life when you were born as the daughter of the Pandya king Malayadhwajan. You ascended the throne and took on the crown. As queen, you fostered and nurtured the Tamil language, celebrated for its prose, poetry, and drama. With radiant pearl bangles on your wrists, you grasped the throat of Lord Siva and controlled the deadly poison he was poised to swallow, in order to save the universe.

notes: The pallavi line “முகுந்தன் மூத்தவளே” (“Elder sister of Mukunda”) is supported by details found in the Srimad Bhagavatam. Vishnu Durga, or Mahamayi, is described as the sister of Lord Vishnu. In his incarnation as Krishna, the Lord instructed her to transfer the fetus from Devaki’s womb to Rohini. He said, “I am going to appear as Krishna, the son of Devaki, endowed with all my divine powers. You will be born as the daughter of Yasoda, ready to be exchanged with the infant Krishna.” Yoga Maya went around him and carried out his command on earth. In Vaishnavite thought, Devi always executes his will instantaneously. Thus, this episode aligns with the idea that Devi is an elder to Krishna—or Mukunda—as described in the pallavi. These events are drawn from Srimad Bhagavatam, Skandha 10, verses 10.2.13–10.2.14. Bhagavan Vishnu also spoke to Devaki, explaining that he had appeared in his divine form to remind her of her previous births, during which she had requested that he be born as her child. He blessed her, saying that in this birth she would relate to him both as her child and as the Supreme Brahman, and would thus ultimately attain his divine feet. After this conversation, he remained still for a few moments and then manifested as an infant before the eyes of the couple (Skandha 10, verses 10.3.44–10.3.47). The above references are from: ஶ்ரீமத் பாகவத ஸாரம், முதல் பாகம், பத்தாவது ஸ்கந்தம், பக்கம் 513, உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, வெளியிடுபவர்: தலைவர், ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004 The pallavi line muNdAsura mardhini refers to the line in Lalitha Tripurasundari sahasranama stotram “chaNda muNdAsura nishUdini”. The Sanskrit line means that Devi killed the Asuras and got the name chAmuNdi. The Charanam of this song has references to illusory acts of Devi or Mahamaya appearing as a cloud and covering the sun to create an illusion that it was sunset, in order to save Partha or Arjuna on the battlefield against Jayadhrutha. It is a generally held belief (including that of this author) by Devi upasakas that all tricks or leelas or illusory mayas performed by Krishna in the Kurukshetra war were due to the divine powers of Yogamayi or Mahamayi. For details of the specific episode, see: Arjuna kills Jayadhrata Jayadhrata's life and death The narrative that Vishnu’s powers made the sun set has been interpreted by people in different ways. The author believes that Vishnu’s sister Vishnu Durga, or Maya, was the divine force who saved Arjuna. The reference for this is in the words of Vyasa in the beginning of the Kurukshetra war, when on the tenth day, Lord Krishna instructed Arjuna to pray to Goddess Durga to win the war and defeat his foes. Arjuna prays to Durga Durga Stuti or Prayers For Tamil version of Vyasa’s verses, see: ஶ்ரீ மஹாபாரத ஸாரம், உரை ஆசிரியர் “அண்ணா”, ஶ்ரீராமகிருஷ்ண மடம், மயிலாப்பூர், சென்னை 600004, ISBN 81-7120-998- X I-2M IC-8-2002, Pages 736-7. Parvathi or Yoga Mayi was born as the seventh child of Devaki. When Kamsa tried to kill her by striking her on the ground, she flew away and warned Kamsa of the impending danger from Krishna, who was already born. This message sent chills through his spine and his evil mind started scheming wicked plots to kill baby Krishna. For details, see: Srimath Bhagavatam, 10th Skantham, verses 10. 4 -12 through 10. 4-43. Goddess Parvathi appeared as a Pandya princess—the daughter of the Pandya king Malayadhwajan—before her marriage to Sundareswara in Madurai. According to the legends of the Meenakshi Amman Temple, the Pandya king ruled Madurai as its capital around 1200 B.C. However, none of the surviving Sangam texts corroborate this timeline, though they do acknowledge the existence of Pandya rulers prior to the period, covered by the extant literature. Malayadhwajan and his wife, Kanchanamalai, remained childless for many years. Following Indra’s suggestion, they performed a Putrakameshti yagna, and Devi Parvathi emerged from the homakundam as an infant. The child bore three breasts from birth. After her father’s death, she ascended the throne, became queen, and conquered several nations. She patronized assemblies of scholars and Tamil poets, during which the Tamil language flourished with the creation of new literary works. For details, see: தடாதகைப் பிராட்டியார் திரு அவதாரப் படலம், தடாதகைப் பிராட்டியாரின் திருமணப் படலம் in கூடல் மாநகரத்து ஆடவல்லான் (திருவிளையாடற் புராண மகிமை), நாகர்கோவில் கிருஷ்ணன், Published by MATHI NILAYAM, #4(39) Thanikachalam Road, Brindavan Apartments, T.Nagar, Chennai 600017, Ph. 4311838, mutaR patippu, 2003, Pages 61 – 108. Devi Parvathi also stopped the spread of the haalahala poison in Lord Siva’s neck when he drank it to save the universe from its deadly effects. This specific episode—of Parvathi restraining the poison—is not fully described in the Mahabharata or in the puranas such as the Bhagavata Purana, Siva Purana, or Padma Purana. However, the sthala puranam and associated legends of the Siva temple at Suruttapalli in the Chittoor district of Andhra Pradesh provide detailed accounts of this event. As Siva gradually began to feel the effects of the poison while traveling toward Kailash, he became extremely drowsy and lay down with his head on Goddess Parvathi’s lap at Suruttapalli. This occurred on a Pradosham day in the early evening, between approximately 4:30 and 6:30 p.m. When he awoke, he saw rishis and devas who had gathered there upon hearing of his condition, and he performed a reenactment of the cosmic dance. The observance of Pradosham is believed to have originated at this very temple, at a time when Siva swallowed the toxin to save the universe. For full details, see: Pallikondeeswara Swamy Temple Sthalapuranam
